---
title: "Cross-Entropy Loss"
description: "A loss function that measures the difference between target and predicted probability distributions."
term: "Cross-Entropy Loss"
letter: "C"
category: "Deep Learning"
difficulty: "Intermediate"
---

## Simple explanation

Cross-entropy loss penalizes a model when it assigns low probability to
the correct class. It is widely used to train classification models.

## Technical explanation

For a target distribution $y$ and predicted distribution $p$, cross-entropy
is $-\sum_i y_i \log p_i$. For a one-hot target, this reduces to the
negative log probability assigned to the correct class. Implementations
often combine log-softmax and negative log-likelihood for numerical
stability.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

The loss function shapes the gradients used to train a classifier. Correctly
matching the loss to the model output and target format is essential;
confusing logits with probabilities or using incompatible label encoding
can cause errors or degraded training.

## How it works

The model produces scores, often called logits. A probability distribution
can be derived from the logits using softmax, and the loss measures the
negative log probability assigned to the target. For a correct class with
probability $p_y$, the loss is $-\log p_y$.

## Practical example

A penguin-versus-ostrich classifier can produce two logits for an image.
Cross-entropy compares those predictions with the known class and gives a
larger penalty when the correct class receives a smaller predicted
probability.

## Common misconceptions

- Cross-entropy is a training objective, not an evaluation metric that
  alone establishes model usefulness.
- Many framework APIs expect raw logits rather than probabilities.
- A low cross-entropy score does not guarantee calibrated probabilities.
